theorems.name: Black-Scholes European Put Formula
theorems.description: Discounted expected put payoff under the risk-neutral lognormal hypothesis: P = K e^{-rT} Phi(-d_2) - S_0 Phi(-d_1), where d_1, d_2 are the standard BS quantities.

import MathFin.BlackScholes.Put

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Real
open scoped NNReal
open MathFin

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}

/-- Black-Scholes European put pricing formula via direct integration
    parallel to the call formula (left-tail completing-the-square). -/
theorem bs_put_formula
    {Q : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure Q]
    {S_0 K r σ T : ℝ} {Z : Ω → ℝ}
    (h : BSCallHyp Q S_0 K r σ T Z) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-r * T) * max (K - bsTerminal S_0 r σ T (Z ω)) 0 ∂Q
      = K * Real.exp (-r * T) * Phi (-(bsd2 S_0 K r σ T)) -
        S_0 * Phi (-(bsd1 S_0 K r σ T)) :=
  MathFin.bs_put_formula h

theorems.name: Black–Scholes Call Is Strictly Convex in the Spot
theorems.description: For K, σ, τ > 0 and any rate r, the Black–Scholes call price S ↦ bsV K r σ S τ = S·Φ(d₁) − Ke^{−rτ}·Φ(d₂) is strictly convex on (0, ∞), and for S₀, s > 0 with s ≠ S₀ it lies strictly above its tangent at S₀, whose slope is the delta Φ(d₁(S₀)): bsV(S₀) + Φ(d₁(S₀))·(s − S₀) < bsV(s). theorems.name: Black–Scholes Call Tends to the Spot as the Volatility Grows

theorems.name: Implied Volatility Exists Above a Reference Volatility
theorems.description: For K, S, T > 0, any rate r and a volatility σ₀ > 0, a call price C strictly between the Black–Scholes price at σ₀ and the spot, bsV K r σ₀ S T < C < S, has an implied volatility σ > σ₀ (bsV K r σ S T = C), and every positive σ' with bsV K r σ' S T = C equals σ. The Black–Scholes price is continuous and strictly increasing in the volatility and tends to S as σ → ∞, so the intermediate value theorem applies. A volatility σ₀ with bsV(σ₀) < C is a hypothesis: existence for every price in the no-arbitrage range ((S − Ke^{−rT})⁺, S) would also need the σ → 0 limit, which is not proved.

Only this direction is proved: that strict convexity on s forces the law to charge every interval of s is not formalized.

theorems.name: Le Floc'h-Kennedy Leading-Order SABR Vol Tends to the Lognormal Vol as nu -> 0
theorems.description: Le Floc'h & Kennedy's leading-order vol omega_0(k) = log(F/k)/Dint(k) is an infinity-times-zero indeterminate form at zero vol-of-vol nu = 0, since their distance Dint(k) = (1/nu)*log(1) there. The removable singularity resolves to omega_0(k) -> -alpha*log(F/k)/y as nu -> 0, nu != 0, for alpha != 0, rho != 1, y != 0 (k != F); at y = -log(F/k) (the beta = 1 case) this limit is exactly alpha, the lognormal vol. The limit is obtained via Dint = nu^-1 * x(-nu*y/alpha), reusing Hagan's x(z) building block and its known slope x'(0) = 1 at the origin.

theorems.name: Dupire Local-Volatility Formula
theorems.description: Dupire's local-vol formula at zero rates, for a driftless X = c + ∫δ dB with δ bounded, adapted and path-continuous (so lognormal models are outside the class): if σ_loc(K)²K² is a continuous version of E[δ_t² | X_t = K] on a strike window and the call surface C(t,K) = E[(X_t − K)⁺] is C² in strike (continuous C_KK) and C¹ in time (jointly continuous C_T), these regularity conditions being assumed, then σ_loc(K)² = 2C_T/(K²C_KK) at every strike of the window with C_KK > 0. Existence of a local-vol diffusion reproducing C is not proved.

import MathFin.BlackScholes.Dupire

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped NNReal

namespace MathFin
open Dupire GyongyMimicry
open ItoIntegralL2 ItoIntegralProcessGeneral

variable {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : Measure Ω} [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]

/-- Dupire's local-volatility formula (Bagaria ch. 9 Thm 9.5, zero rates): on a strike
window where the call surface is `C²` in strike and `C¹` in calendar time and `C_KK > 0`,
a lognormal-convention local volatility satisfies
`σloc(K)² = 2·∂_T C(t, K) / (K²·∂²_K C(t, K))` at every strike of the window with
`C_KK > 0`. -/
theorem dupire_local_vol_ratio
    {B : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (hB : IsPreBrownianReal B μ) (hBmeas : ∀ t, Measurable (B t))
    {T : ℝ≥0} {δ : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ}
    (hδadap : ∀ t, StronglyMeasurable[natFiltration hBmeas t] (δ t))
    (hδcont : ∀ ω, Continuous fun s : ℝ≥0 ↦ δ s ω)
    {Dd : ℝ} (hδbdd : ∀ t ω, |δ t ω| ≤ Dd)
    {M : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ}
    (hMadap : ∀ t, StronglyMeasurable[natFiltration hBmeas t] (M t))
    (hMeq : ∀ t, M t =ᵐ[μ] (itoProcessCLM hB T t hBmeas
      (processToLp T hBmeas hδadap hδcont hδbdd) : Ω → ℝ))
    {X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → ℝ} (c : ℝ)
    (hXcont : ∀ ω, Continuous fun s : ℝ≥0 ↦ X s ω)
    (hXrel : ∀ t : ℝ≥0, X t = fun ω : Ω ↦ c + M t ω)
    (t : ℝ) (ht : 0 < t) (htT : Real.toNNReal t < T)
    {a b ε : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) (hε : 0 < ε) {CK CKK : ℝ → ℝ} {Ct : ℝ → ℝ → ℝ}
    (hCK : ∀ K ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt (callSurface μ X t) (CK K) K)
    (hCKK : ∀ K ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt CK (CKK K) K)
    (hCKKc : ContinuousOn CKK (Ioo a b))
    (hCt : ∀ s ∈ Ioo (t - ε) (t + ε), ∀ K ∈ Ioo a b,
      HasDerivAt (fun s' => callSurface μ X s' K) (Ct s K) s)
    (hCtc : ContinuousOn (Function.uncurry Ct) (Ioo (t - ε) (t + ε) ×ˢ Ioo a b))
    {σloc : ℝ → ℝ} (hσc : ContinuousOn σloc (Ioo a b))
    (hσrep : ∀ᵐ ω ∂μ, X (Real.toNNReal t) ω ∈ Ioo a b →
      diffCoeffSq μ (reindexed X) (reindexed δ) t ω
        = σloc (X (Real.toNNReal t) ω) ^ 2 * X (Real.toNNReal t) ω ^ 2) :
    ∀ K ∈ Ioo a b, 0 < CKK K → σloc K ^ 2 = 2 * Ct t K / (K ^ 2 * CKK K) :=
  MathFin.Dupire.dupire_pointwise hB hBmeas hδadap hδcont hδbdd hMadap hMeq c hXcont hXrel
    t ht htT ha hε hCK hCKK hCKKc hCt hCtc hσc hσrep

end MathFin

theorems.name: Heston Affine-Transform Pricing PDE
theorems.description: The 2D exponential-affine ansatz for the Heston model satisfies the pricing PDE: with Bx constant and Bv, A the explicit rho-shifted Riccati closed forms, d/ds Phi(s,x,v) + L Phi(s,x,v) = 0 at every (s,x,v), where L is the Heston generator (r - v/2) d_x + kappa(theta - v) d_v + (v/2) d_xx + rho xi v d_xv + (xi^2 v/2) d_vv. Strip: 0 < u < 1, xi != 0. That this profile equals E[e^{u log S_T}] is not proved; the Heston process is not constructed.

import MathFin.BlackScholes.Heston

open scoped NNReal

namespace MathFin
open Heston

/-- The Heston pricing PDE at the explicit affine transform: the calendar-time
profile built from the rho-shifted Riccati closed forms solves
`d/ds Phi + L Phi = 0` against the Heston generator. -/
theorem heston_affine_pde (r κ θ ξ ρ u T : ℝ) (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) (hu1 : 0 < u)
    (hu2 : u < 1) (t x v : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun s => hestonProfile u (fun w => hestonA r κ θ ξ ρ u (T - w))
        (fun w => hestonBv κ ξ ρ u (T - w)) s x v) t
      + hestonGenerator r κ θ ξ ρ (hestonProfile u (fun w => hestonA r κ θ ξ ρ u (T - w))
          (fun w => hestonBv κ ξ ρ u (T - w)) t) x v = 0 :=
  MathFin.Heston.hestonTransform_pde r κ θ ξ ρ u T hξ hu1 hu2 t x v

end MathFin
